title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). S is a connected scheme of finite type over Q (by normality one may reduce to S = Spec K, with K finitely generated over Q). A is a finitely generated abelian group with a map A -> G_m(S), and T = \hat{Z}(1) = lim mu_n. Extracting all n-th roots of the elements of A defines a Kummer torsor, hence a Kummer map pi_1(S) -> Hom(A,T). On pi_1 this map is only a crossed homomorphism. On pi_1^+ (the kernel of the cyclotomic character, whose image Gamma in \hat{Z}^* is open) it is a genuine homomorphism, with image \tilde{pi}_1^+.

On this page. Put \check{A} = Hom_Z(A,Z), which is free of rank n = rk A. Since T is torsion-free, Hom_Z(A,T) is canonically \check{A} ⊗ T = \check{A}(1), which is isomorphic to \hat{Z}^n, though not canonically (357).

Grothendieck wants to prove that \tilde{pi}_1^+ is open in \check{A}(1). He then asks a stronger question. Take S_1 normal, connected, of finite type and dominant over Z, set A = H^0(S_1, G_m) and S = S_{1,Q}. Is pi_1(S) -> \check{A}(1) necessarily surjective? More generally, should it be surjective whenever G_m(S)/Im A is torsion-free? He notes that under hypothesis (355) one can always reach this case by enlarging A to A' ⊂ H^0(S,G_m) with A'/A finite.

The next page specializes to S = Spec Q, where G_m(Q) = Q^* = {±1} × Z^{(P)}. There he asks two things about the Kummer characters zeta_p : Gamma_Q^+ -> \hat{Z}(1): (a) are they surjective or open, and (b) are they \hat{Z}-independent? The problem served is to understand the size of \tilde{pi}_1^+, motivated by an earlier 'Fermat' context with p = 2.
errors: Openness of the image of pi_1^+ is correct. For K finitely generated over Q and A injecting into K^*/mu(K), the Kummer image of Gal(\bar K/K(mu_infty)) in Hom(A, \hat Z(1)) is open; this is classical Kummer theory.

Surjectivity, read for pi_1^+ (as on the next page), is false even when G_m(S)/Im A is torsion-free. Take S_1 = Spec Z[1/2] and A = {±1} × 2^Z. Then Q^*/A is free, but sqrt 2 lies in Q(zeta_8), so the image of Gamma_Q^+ in Hom(A, \hat Z(1)) has index 2. More generally Q^ab = Q(mu_infty), so every quadratic Kummer character vanishes on Gamma_Q^+. The 2-adic part of the image therefore lies in 2·Hom, giving index 2^n for n independent primes. The odd part is surjective.

Read literally for the whole pi_1, the Kummer map is a crossed homomorphism, so 'surjective' means surjective as a map of sets. In the Z[1/2] example that set-theoretic surjectivity actually holds, by compensating with the cyclotomic part. The question is only sharp for pi_1^+, which is how Grothendieck treats it on the next page.

ideas.what: Canonical identification Hom_Z(A, \hat Z(1)) = \check A ⊗ \hat Z(1) for A finitely generated (torsion in A drops out)
Openness of the image of Gal(\bar K/K(mu_infty)) in Hom(A, \hat Z(1)) under the Kummer map, for finitely generated A ⊂ K^* and K finitely generated over Q
ideas.modern_name: Open image theorem in Kummer theory (Bashmakov, Schinzel, Ribet 1979; later Perucca and others on Kummer degrees)

ideas.what: Question whether the Kummer map is surjective when the cokernel G_m(S)/A is torsion-free, e.g. A = global units of an arithmetic scheme S_1
ideas.modern_name: Index of the Kummer image / entanglement with cyclotomic fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (failure via quadratic subfields of cyclotomic fields, Kronecker–Weber)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine Kummer-theoretic question whose answer is classical. Openness of the image is known. Surjectivity on pi_1^+ fails because of the 2-adic obstruction sqrt(±p) ∈ Q(mu_{4p}), which Grothendieck himself seems about to meet on the following pages. Nothing new for specialists.
